facts.text: Camilla was named after the granddaughter of Henry Mitchell, a Revolutionary War general after whom Mitchell County was named.
The town’s courthouse, built in 1858, was the site of the 1868 Camilla Massacre and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The Pelham Historic Carnegie Library, one of only 24 Carnegie libraries in Georgia, still serves the community and showcases beautiful early 20th‑century architecture.
A group of six Live Oak trees over 200 years old in Camilla’s green space are registered as landmark and historic trees by the Georgia Urban Forest Council.
Camilla’s mild winters are due to its southerly latitude, giving it a more tropical climate than cities farther north like Atlanta.
In 1858, Camilla was incorporated and became the county seat of Mitchell County, anchoring its role as the region’s administrative center.
